answer: Storage is bound to identity by a replication proof that is hard to satisfy with shared bytes, and because the sealed data is unique per identity, aliases and thin-provisioned clones fail the proof at their next challenge. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns an echo, answers a lagoon, and is named by a vine: a farm can mint vine bindings instantly, but the echo behind each one is disk, and the lagoon will catch the ones that share it. Proof-of-replication only bounds the attack instead of blocking it.
